1.name: RO
1.hint: receiver output, high impedance while RE is high (p. 7); high when A − B > 200 mV, low when < −200 mV, high with open inputs (p. 10); VOH ≥ 3.5 V at 4 mA – a 5 V level into a 3.3 V microcontroller

3.name: DE
3.hint: driver output enable, active high (p. 7); no internal pull is stated – a floating DE at reset leaves the bus undefined

6.name: A
6.hint: non-inverting receiver input and driver output; bus pin: absolute maximum −8 V … +12.5 V; receiver specified for −7 V ≤ VCM ≤ 12 V; input resistance ≥ 12 kΩ = one unit load (32 per bus); driver high impedance while DE is low

7.name: B
7.hint: inverting receiver input and driver output; bus pin: absolute maximum −8 V … +12.5 V; receiver specified for −7 V ≤ VCM ≤ 12 V; input resistance ≥ 12 kΩ = one unit load (32 per bus); driver high impedance while DE is low

hints: 5 V part: VCC 4.75–5.25 V (p. 7); the MAX3485 is the 3.3 V counterpart with the same pinout

RS-485 bus: terminate the line at both ends in its characteristic impedance and keep stubs short (Figures 21–22 show 120 Ω at each end); the data sheet names no fail-safe bias for an idle terminated bus – its receiver fail-safe covers open inputs only (p. 13)

half duplex: DE and RE# select transmit or receive; with DE low and RE# high both outputs are released (the MAX485 has no shutdown mode, p. 11); up to 2.5 Mbps, drivers not slew-rate limited (p. 1, p. 3)
driver short-circuit current 35–250 mA over −7 … 12 V, thermal shutdown releases the driver outputs (p. 3, p. 11)
idd_max_a 0.9 mA is the no-load supply current with DE high (p. 3); a driver into a terminated bus draws its load current on top

pin description and Figure 1 (8-pin DIP/SO), p. 7

pin v_max_v 12.5 on RO, RE#, DE, DI: VCC + 0.5 V at the absolute maximum VCC 12 V (computed from p. 2); the bound to the actual supply is vin_rel_max_v 0.5

switching characteristics MAX485, p. 3: maximum data rate 2.5 Mbps
function tables, p. 10: driver outputs and RO high impedance when disabled; RO high with inputs open
line length and termination, p. 13; unit loads (12 kΩ = 1 unit load, 32 transceivers), p. 8
